raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On SM100, `fused_q` now writes the DSA indexer weights directly in BF16, the dtype DeepGEMM's MQA logits kernels
take. This removes the FP32 to BF16 copy `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` launched on every indexer call.

## Claims

- InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4x GB200: together with #62171 and #62172, decode time per turn
  drops 2.8%, 2.5%, 1.5% and 1.5% at concurrency 1, 4, 8 and 16 (main vs main: within 0.7%). This PR is
  about 1/6 of that.
- One fewer kernel per indexer call (prefill chunks and decode) on SM100/SM103 for DSA models using `fused_q`
  (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x).
- No precision change. The SM100 logits kernels only take BF16 weights, so main already rounds them to BF16 with a
  separate `.to(torch.bfloat16)` in [`mqa_logits_mx_inputs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd/vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py#L635). `fused_q` now
  does that rounding in its store, and the kernels get bit-identical weights.
- Other platforms are unchanged (FP32 weights).

## Validation

- `tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py` on B300 (SM103): 214 passed, 8 skipped. The weight
  assertions now check BF16 output on SM100 and FP32 elsewhere.
- Bit-identity on B300: for 5.3M weights (Triton and CuTeDSL kernels, GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V3.2 shapes, 1 to 4096
  tokens), the BF16 output matches main's FP32 output followed by `.to(torch.bfloat16)` in every bit.
- InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4x GB200, main + #62170, #62171 and #62172 vs main (median per-turn change
  on the same turns, 95% CI; setup below):

  | concurrency | 1 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | decode time | -2.8% [-3.1, -2.6] | -2.5% [-3.1, -1.7] | -1.5% [-2.2, -1.1] | -1.5% [-2.4, +0.3] |
  | e2e latency | -3.3% [-3.9, -3.0] | -1.8% [-2.7, -0.9] | -1.2% [-2.0, -0.5] | -0.6% [-1.9, +2.4] |
  | KV cache tokens | +0.2% | +0.7% | +1.4% | 0 |
  | main vs main, decode | -0.1% | -0.7% | +0.3% | -0.3% |

- Target verify forward (`vllm bench forward`, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, B300, MTP verify shapes, spread < 0.1%):
  -0.18% to -0.34% at 1, 3 and 7 requests, 25K and 94K context.
- Exactness: with real MTP verification on 32 GSM8K questions (greedy), the three changes together give the same
  outputs and the same acceptance length (3.4904) as main.
- MRCR (OpenAI, 8 needles, 594 samples), GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4x GB200, TP4, greedy, thinking off; main vs main +
  #62170, #62171 and #62172. Difference is the paired per-sample mean with a 95% bootstrap CI:

  | context | ≤8K | ≤16K | ≤32K | ≤64K | ≤128K | ≤256K | all |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | main | 0.925 | 0.904 | 0.934 | 0.898 | 0.904 | 0.852 | 0.903 |
  | with the PRs | 0.934 | 0.917 | 0.915 | 0.924 | 0.885 | 0.767 | 0.890 |
  | difference | +0.009 | +0.014 | -0.019 | +0.025 | -0.018 | -0.085 | -0.013 |
  | 95% CI | [-0.029, +0.047] | [-0.035, +0.063] | [-0.068, +0.029] | [-0.033, +0.084] | [-0.085, +0.048] | [-0.174, +0.007] | [-0.038, +0.012] |

  The 256K bin varies between runs, so it was run twice more for each:

  | ≤256K | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | main | 0.852 | 0.732 | 0.732 |
  | with the PRs | 0.767 | 0.743 | 0.750 |

  Pooled over the three runs, the difference is -0.019 [-0.069, +0.031].

<details>
<summary>InferenceX AgentX setup and results for all GLM-5.3 PRs (4x GB200)</summary>

InferenceX c801c9f2d AgentX scenario (pinned AIPerf), 20-minute fast mode, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 rev e3b8f9f2, TP4, MTP 3
with synthetic acceptance 2.99, native KV offload 135 GB per rank, Rust frontend, `max-num-seqs` = 2 x
concurrency. vLLM main dcd07967ca with its default backends and CUDA graph config, plus the PRs cumulatively in
the order below (FlashInfer with flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631 and
flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6632 from #62174 on). One FlashInfer MoE autotune per concurrency, shared by all
variants. A fresh server per point, with the page cache dropped before each, and main run again at the end of
each concurrency as an A/A check. SGLang a916d91cd3 with IMEX, TRT-LLM
all-reduce fusion and `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`.

Each cell is the median, over the turns both runs finished (150 to 520), of the per-turn ratio to the previous
variant, with a 95% paired bootstrap CI. Decode is request latency minus TTFT. The bootstrap does not include
run-to-run variance; the main-vs-main row does.

| decode time per turn | c=1 | c=4 | c=8 | c=16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| + #62170, #62171, #62172 | -2.8% [-3.1, -2.6] | -2.5% [-3.1, -1.7] | -1.5% [-2.2, -1.1] | -1.5% [-2.4, +0.3] |
| + #62174 | -1.6% [-1.8, -1.5] | -1.8% [-2.5, -0.9] | -3.3% [-3.9, -2.9] | -2.1% [-3.8, -0.9] |
| + #62173 | +0.5% (no-op here) | -0.3% [-0.5, -0.1] | -0.1% [-0.4, +0.3] | -0.9% [-2.0, +0.2] |
| all PRs vs main | -3.7% [-3.9, -3.5] | -4.3% [-4.8, -4.0] | -5.3% [-6.4, -4.8] | -4.8% [-6.5, -3.8] |
| main vs main (noise) | -0.1% | -0.7% | +0.3% | -0.3% |

| e2e latency per turn | c=1 | c=4 | c=8 | c=16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| + #62170, #62171, #62172 | -3.3% | -1.8% | -1.2% | -0.6% |
| + #62174 | -1.4% | -1.4% | -2.7% | -1.6% |
| + #62173 | +0.9% | -0.3% | -0.7% | -1.1% |
| all PRs vs main | -4.1% | -3.4% | -4.7% | -3.8% |
| main vs main (noise) | -0.6% | -1.2% | +0.4% | -0.4% |

KV cache tokens per GPU (c=1 / 4 / 8 / 16): main 1,176,832 / 1,162,880 / 1,143,872 / 1,105,984; with all PRs
1,178,496 / 1,168,512 / 1,157,824 / 1,103,936. Window throughput (tok/s/GPU) moves up to 2.4% between runs in fast
mode, since it counts whichever long-context turns finish inside the 20 minutes; with all PRs it is +3.0%, -1.4%,
+4.8% and +1.2% at c=1/4/8/16.

vLLM vs SGLang, decode time per turn on the same turns (positive = vLLM slower):

| | c=1 | c=4 | c=8 | c=16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | +10.4% | +12.7% | +13.7% | -2.9% |
| all PRs | +6.2% | +7.5% | +5.7% | -6.9% |

#62170, #62171 and #62172 were measured as one group. `vllm bench forward` (target verify forward, spread < 0.1%)
splits their gain about 1/6, 1/2 and 1/3. #62173 changes only decode steps of 3, 5 or 7 requests; steps with 3 or
more requests are 0%, 4%, 13% and 37% of all steps at c=1/4/8/16. At c=1 both runs capture the same graphs, so
its +0.5% there is noise. At c=16, three more runs each of + #62174 and + #62173 (4 runs each, compared as
runs): decode time -0.54% [-0.93, -0.16], with every + #62173 run faster than every + #62174 run (permutation
p = 2/70); e2e latency -0.29% [-1.41, +0.82].

</details>

## Details

`mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()` already decides that the SM100 logits kernels take BF16 weights, and
`mqa_logits_mx_inputs` returned `weights.to(torch.bfloat16)`. That was a real copy kernel for every indexer call,
since `fused_q` (Triton and CuTeDSL) always wrote FP32. `fused_q` now allocates its weights output in the dtype the
logits kernels take, and both kernels cast on store. `.to(torch.bfloat16)` then returns the tensor as-is.

The CuTeDSL kernel's compile key gains the output dtype.

issue_comments.body: Same answer as on #62172: main already rounds these weights to BF16 in [`mqa_logits_mx_inputs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd/vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py#L635), since the SM100 logits kernels only take BF16. This PR just moves that rounding into `fused_q`. The output is bit-identical (5.3M weights checked, 0 mismatches), and the MRCR run in #62172 covers this PR too.
